items.caption: Dear orchestrator of the Christmas Magic …. Want to do it together??
items.transcript: You will have someone in your house that is like the orchestrator of the Christmas magic. It's probably you because you're watching this video right now. And everyone else in your house, especially if you've got kids, thinks that Christmas, it just happens. They just wake up on Christmas Eve and the house smells lovely and there's all sorts of lovely things happening and there's lovely food and there's presents and there's activities. Someone has to have made that happen. It's probably you. Christmas carries an enormous mental load. For that one person to carry around, it can be intense, especially if you're trying to do it all at the same time. It's going to leave you stressed. It's going to leave you feeling like your brain has just got off the waltzes. So if we can spread it out, it doesn't make it any less mental loady, right? But it's going to spread it out so it's much less intense for your brain.

items.caption: THIS is why we start Organised Christmas in September …. #theorganisedmum #mentalload #organisedchristmas
items.transcript: If you assign like an hour, hour and a half max each week over the next two or three months to a little bit of Christmas planning, a little bit of Christmas prep, you're going to be able to slot it into your life easy. You can prep almost by stealth without you even realizing it and without it having a massive impact on your life. If you leave it to the last minute, it could be that you have to take, I take two or three days off work just to make, to clean the house and to prep. We're going to be doing all of that over time. And Christmas is expensive, right? Thinking about presents, thinking about things that you want to do, buying travel early before it becomes expensive. You're spreading the cost and also you're going to buy intentionally as well. So it's going to reduce the amount of panic buying that you are doing. Which is all going to save you money.

items.caption:
You are NOT behind. September just likes to make you feel like you are.
Everyone suddenly seems to be back in September mode. School’s back. Work’s back. The calendar is filling up. The group chats are pinging. And meanwhile you’re wondering why you haven’t magically slipped straight back right into it. 

Remember: your routine didn’t fail over summer. The conditions that supported it disappeared.
For six weeks, the timings changed. People were home who usually weren’t. Meals moved. Bedtimes moved. The school run vanished. Your normal little anchors throughout the day weren’t there. So don’t respond by trying to overhaul your entire life this week.

Give normal life a few days to happen again.
Let the school runs, work days, meal times and usual weekly commitments fall back into place and THEN look at where the friction is.
What keeps getting forgotten? Where are the bottlenecks? What part of the day feels chaotic? What actually needs a new system?
Build your routine around the life you’re living now, rather than desperately trying to get back to the one you had before summer.

You’re just finding your new rhythm. Love Gem ❤️❤️
items.transcript: The first thing you need to wrap your head around is the fact that you have not fallen behind. You were just dealing with a different set of circumstances whilst the kids were at home. Your life changed for six weeks. You haven't just fallen off the routine. The circumstances around your routine changed. Your usual daily scaffold of get up, breakfast, school run, out the house, it completely disappeared. That is completely different to falling off a routine. The conditions left you.

items.caption:
🎉🎄WEEK 1 And we’re OFF!!!! Welcome to #organisedchristmas Here’s your list of tasks for this week 🎉

❤️Pick the bits the apply and ditch the rest! Remember if you want a handy customisable tick list then we’ve got you covered over in @the_organised_method 

Ok yours tasks .... 

🎄For those of you who followed along last year, dig out your xmas audit and arm yourself with your findings from last December to keep you on track. We love a bit of data! 

🎄Look into supermarket delivery savers, if you don’t use one it is time to sort your supermarket delivery saver. Christmas slots go fast. Sign up for a delivery saver pass if you can to help you grab your slot before the rest of the world beats you to it.

🎄Get booking Santa and Christmas events NOW. The good ones sell out. Panto? Ice skating? Winter markets? This is your year. Book now to spread the cost and avoid the disappointment of sold-out shows.

🎄Plan Christmas get-togethers. Pick a date, send save-the-date cards/texts/emails. Remember to sort the babysitters. Diaries fill up frighteningly fast from October onwards.

🎄Book Christmas travel. Train and flight prices only go one way the closer you get. Book now and thank yourself later.

🎄Order Advent calendars. Yes, already! Beauty, chocolate, candles. The good ones sell out well before December. Order now and save yourself the scramble. If your fave isn’t on sale yet, set a reminder and circle back.

🎄Start putting any money you can spare to one side now to help with the budget.

Ok we’re under way :) See you next week! Gem ❤️❤️❤️❤️

items.caption: So many people underestimate the tax all constant context switching, micro managing and ‘5 min jobs’ take on our brain. And you get to the end of the day and wonder why you’re tired?? THIS is why you’re drained by 8pm.
items.transcript: Sometimes you can get to the end of the day and you think, what on earth have I done? You felt super busy, but you can't quite pin down what has been keeping you busy. Maybe you found someone's swimming goggles. It could be that you mopped up someone else's mistake at work. Found someone's charger. You made dinner. None of these things individually is a massive job. And that is exactly the problem. Your day has been chopped into tiny little pieces. And I think we massively underestimate the cost of that. Running a home doesn't just take your time. It also takes a lot of your attention.

items.caption: This is exactly what we’re talking about in today’s Daily Clean inside @the_organised_method Come and do your 30 minutes with me 💋#cleaningmotivation
items.transcript: I want to have a little word with you about the fantasy version of yourself. I think she might be ruining your week. Fantasy you is the woman that you think is going to appear at 9.30 at night and handle all of the washing, all of the admin that you haven't kept up with in the day, reset the kitchen for the morning. Except when that time comes, fantasy you is nowhere to be seen. And it's just actual you. Actual you is knackered, you're stood in the kitchen and there's a high potential you might be eating grated cheese out of the packet. And this is one of the biggest mistakes that I see people make when they are trying to get organised. They don't plan for their actual lives. They think about all of the shoulds. A system that only works when you're operating at 100% isn't a very good system. Your home and your routines need to be locked in for the real version of you. Your real energy, your real time and your very, very real circumstances.

items.caption: Does your mind still race when you’re sitting down? Do you jump up from the sofa when someone walks in because you feel guilty for being ‘caught’ resting? 👀😩 You don’t need to earn your rest ❤️
items.transcript: I think many of us have absorbed this idea that being busy is evidence of being good. A good parent is doing, they're playing, a good partner is anticipating, a good homeowner is maintaining, a good woman particularly seems to be permanently en route to another task. Even when we sit down, part of us mentally remains standing. We are like scanning the room, we remember the appointment, we notice the finger marks on the window. The body may be on the sofa but your mind is still walking around your house with a clipboard. And because domestic work is so visible when it's not been done, it can make everything feel almost confrontational, like the washing basket sat in the corner of the room is like a witness for the prosecution. But you know what? Rest is not a reward that you claim after a sufficiently productive day. You don't have to prove that you have done enough to qualify for it.

items.caption: How to switch cleaning maintenance mode! #cleaningroutine
items.transcript: Really, really quickly, if you want to ditch the big reset to Sunday resets, you need to work out how much time you realistically have every single week. So sit down, work out where are my pockets of time. It doesn't matter if they're just 10, 15, 30 minutes a day. Work out where they realistically are. Realistically, not what you think you should have, what you actually have. And then you need to work out what are the priority top level jobs that you need to be doing in your house that are going to keep things ticking over to stop things sliding backwards, right? The idea is we're going to switch you from reactive resets to proactive maintenance cleaning. That is what we want to do. So once you've worked out the time, what you need to do, you should be having a real quick scaffold, a nice bird's eye look at what your house needs on a weekly basis, which coincidentally is how the organized method is designed to how it works. We will guide you through making sure that you are doing that in your house every week. But you've got to work with the time and the energy and the things that your house needs weekly.

items.caption:
A to-do list tells you what needs doing but a DREAD list tells you what’s quietly taking up space in your head.

These jobs are rarely particularly difficult. But every time you remember one and decide not to do it, your brain has to carry it for a little longer.

So write down everything you’ve been avoiding and pick one thing to deal with today.

Not the whole list (This isn’t a punishment). Just one small job you can finally stop thinking about.

The task might take ten minutes. The relief tends to last much longer. Get it down in the comments and then GET IT DONE ⚡️🙌
items.transcript: Come here if you have a dread list. Not a to-do list, a dread list. A list of the things that you just don't want to do and you've just been putting it off for far too long. Small jobs that you've been quietly carrying around in your brain. I want to do them, like booking the dentist, sending that email, turning the parcels. None of them are enormous, but when they all add up they can feel really, really draining. Today I've got a little bit of a challenge for you. I want you just to write it all down and I just want you to get one item off it. Kill it. Quite often the job itself can take like 10 minutes. It's the carrying it around in our brain for three weeks, three months that is the exhausting part. Once you've chosen it, tell me what it is below and we can all cheer each other on. I am going to be booking my hygiene appointment at the dentist. Not because I'm scared of the dentist, it's because I'm just not quite getting around to doing it and every single morning I wake up and go, ah, must do that. I am going to do it today.

items.caption:
Ready to get out of your constantly-looking-for-a-new-cleaning-routine era? Because I promise you, the answer probably isn’t another routine.

It’s very easy to get stuck in the cycle of finding a new system, feeling wildly motivated for three days, missing a day and then deciding the whole thing doesn’t work.

But a good routine shouldn’t require perfect conditions to keep it going. It needs to work when you’re busy. When the kids are home and when work is ridiculously hectic. 

The aim isn’t to find a routine you can follow perfectly. It’s to find one you can come back to easily. And one that is realistic enough that you’re not forever feeling behind. That’s the bit we sometimes miss.

You don’t need another fresh start. You need something boringly reliable that gives you more time to get on with your actual life.

And yes, that is pretty much why I created TOM.
Don’t pay attention to what you can do in a big house reset, instead pay attention to the normal days becuase that’s where the real data lives ❤️❤️❤️
items.transcript: It doesn't really matter what your house looks like after a two hour Sunday, Monday, Friday, whenever reset. It matters what it looks like on a regular Monday afternoon or a regular Tuesday morning. You've not done anything special. That is the real test. It's going to give you so much data, so much information. It's going to let you know whether your house is running smoothly, if it's running organised, what energy do you really have, what time do you really have without you having to have these pockets of bursts of like mad energy to do a reset. Because we can all do that and it looks great for 30 minutes afterwards, but is it sustainable?
